texts.preamble: Narayana Shantha vs Taluk Medical Officer on 20 July, 2018 Author: Aravind Kumar Bench: Aravind Kumar 1 In The High Court Of Karnataka At Bengaluru Dated This The 20th Day Of July, 2018 Before The Hon'Ble Mr.Justice Aravind Kumar W.P.No. 10981/2018 (Gm-Res) Between: Narayana Shantha S/O Late Manku Shantha Aged About 68 Years Priya Enterprises Shantha House Paneer Kondana Derlakatte Village And Post Mangalore Taluk D.K.District - 575 001 ... Petitioner (By Sri. Ravi Kumar G.H., Advocate For Sri Sachin B.S., Advocate) And: 1 Taluk Medical Officer Health And Family Welfare Department Mangalore Taluk D.K.-575001. 2 Competent Authority Food Safety And Standard Act Attavar, Mangalore 575 001 D.K. District. ... Respondents
texts.facts: ORDER Petitioner has questioned the order dated 07.09.2017 passed by first respondent directing the petitioner to obtain license from District Health Officer, Food Safety and Standards Act and notice dated 06.07.2017-Annexure-B issued by second respondent calling upon the petitioner to obtain license from Indian Standard Institute and Bureau of Indian Standards, failing which petitioner has been directed to close the unit forthwith. 3. Petitioner is claiming to be a registered drinking water supplier and is said to have been supplying water after obtaining permission from local authority namely, Town Panchayath Office and Health Officer, Health Department, Dakshina Kannada. It is contended that petitioner's unit is a non-packaged drinking water unit and therefore, obtaining certificates from Indian Standard Institution and Bureau of Indian Standards for commencement or running of drinking water purifying unit would not arise and as such, respondents have no authority to issue the impugned order/notice. Hence, he prays for allowing the writ petition. 4. This Court, in writ petition Nos.14176 to 180/2018 and connected matters had an occasion to consider similar plea and after noticing the Division Bench judgment of this Court in the case of LOCHAMESH B. HUGAR vs UNION OF INDIA, MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE DEPARTMENT AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2013 KAR 306 had issued certain directions to the petitioners therein by observing: "8. In the light of said directions issued by the Division Bench and affidavits now having been filed by the petitioners herein undertaking to obtain certificate from Bureau of Indian Standards, this Court is of the considered view that petitioners are selling the water though not under packaged container but by cans, the fact remains that said water is being sold for human consumption and as such, petitioners cannot be heard to contend that they need not obtain BIS certification." Said observations would be squarely applicable to the facts on hand. In view of learned Advocate appearing for petitioner undertaking to file affidavit of the petitioner on similar lines, this court is of the considered view, this writ petition can also be disposed of on the lines of the order passed by this court on 27.06.2018 in W.P.Nos.14176-180/2018 & 14638/2018 whereunder it was ordered as follows: "9. In that view of the matter, by placing the affidavits of undertaking given by the petitioners on record and contentions raised by learned Advocate appearing for petitioners that petitioners may be directed to obtain certification from Chief Food Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Public Health Institute Building, Sheshadri Road, K.R.Circle, Bengaluru who shall certify as to the potability of water being sold by the petitioners, these writ petitions can be disposed of. Hence, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER (1) Writ petitions stand disposed of reserving liberty to petitioners to file applications before the Chief Food Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Public Health Institute Building, Sheshadri Road, K.R.Circle, Bengaluru within two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order and on receipt of said applications, said authority shall examine the same and issue certificate about potability of the water being sold by the petitioners. (2) On such certificate being obtained and produced by the petitioners before third respondent, he shall forthwith restore possession of the units to the petitioner and permit them to use/run the units and shall immediately lift the seizure of petitioners' units. (3) For the purpose of obtaining sample water from the units, third respondent shall open the lock and enable the petitioner to provide water sample as they desire to obtain water from the unit and produce the same before the Chief Food Analyst for being analysed and certified. (4) Petitioners shall also submit applications to the Bureau of Indian Standards as prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulations made thereunder and as provided under Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 for issuance of certificate for manufacture/sale of water within three weeks from the date of receipt of certification from the Chief Food Analyst as ordered hereinabove. (5) Since Bureau of Indian Standards is not a party to these proceedings, no further direction is issued to Bureau of Indian Standards and it would be open to the petitioners to pursue their application before Bureau of Indian Standards for being processed in accordance with law. (2) On such certificate being obtained and produced by the petitioner before second respondent, it shall forthwith restore possession of the unit to the petitioner and permit him to use/run the unit and shall immediately thereof lift the seizure of petitioner's unit. (3) For the purpose of obtaining sample water from the unit, second respondent shall open the lock to enable the petitioner to provide water sample as he so desires to obtain water from the unit and produce the same before the Chief Food Analyst for being analysed and certified.
